statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-13034: with QUIC through ngtcp2 built on GnuTLS, curl skipped the CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY (--pinnedpubkey) check when standard certificate verification was disabled, so an impostor server went unnoticed. curl 8.8.0 to 8.17.0 are affected and 8.18.0 fixes it: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2025-13034.html, https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/3d91ca8cdb3b434226e743946d428b4dd3acf2c9. Debian fixed it for trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 by cherry-picking that commit: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-13034. The affected code ships in libcurl3t64-gnutls, whose libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 links libngtcp2 and libngtcp2_crypto_gnutls. Unpacked all 51 binary packages published from the curl source in the DHI Debian repository: curl 8.14.1 in its three published Debian revisions, built from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 sources, for amd64 and arm64, namely curl, libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libcurl4-gnutls-dev and libcurl4-doc, and the debug-symbol packages curl-dbgsym, libcurl4t64-dbgsym and libcurl3t64-gnutls-dbgsym. Their ELF files are the curl program and the libcurl.so.4.8.0 (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 (GnuTLS) shared libraries, each dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, plus detached debug-information files in the debug-symbol packages. The development packages also ship the static archives libcurl.a and libcurl-gnutls.a, each with 179 members that are all libcurl's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file. Every published build is built from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 or 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 source, and the Debian changelog shipped in each records the 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 entry 'd/p/CVE-2025-13034.patch: cherry-pick from upstream', so every published build carries the fix. The range therefore ends at the lowest published build. Earlier builds from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u2 source, which predate the fix, are no longer published and sort below that bound.
